frames.narration: The user starts a word count over a large set of files. The library splits the input into M pieces of 16 MB to 64 MB and starts many copies of the program. One copy becomes the master. It keeps a table of every map task and reduce task and whether each is idle, in progress or completed.

messages.label: run the job: M map tasks, R reduce tasks

frames.narration: The master gives a map task to an idle worker, preferring one that already holds a copy of that piece of input in GFS, or one near it, so the input is mostly read locally and uses no network bandwidth.

The map worker calls the map function for each line, which emits (word, 1) pairs. A combiner adds repeated words up locally, so ('the', 1) many times becomes one ('the', 37). The worker buffers the pairs and writes them to its own local disk, divided into R regions by hash(word) mod R.

The master tells the reduce worker for region 3 where those regions are. The reduce worker reads its region from every map worker's disk over the network, then sorts all the pairs by word, so that every pair for one word is next to the others.

messages.label: read region 3 from each map worker

frames.narration: The reduce worker calls the reduce function once per word with the list of its counts, and writes the totals to a temporary file in GFS. When it finishes, it renames the file to its final name. A rename is atomic, so a second run of the same task cannot leave a half-written file.

Now a map worker dies. Its pings go unanswered, so the master marks it failed. Its finished map tasks go back to idle, because their output was on its local disk, which can no longer be read. The master gives them to other workers. Its finished reduce tasks stay finished, since their output is in GFS.

Near the end, one reduce task on a slow machine is still running. The master starts a backup copy of it on another worker. Whichever copy finishes first completes the task, and the other result is ignored. This is the paper's answer to stragglers, which made its sort 44% slower when turned off.

messages.label: run a backup copy of the last tasks
